To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the highest polarization entanglement tolerance to PMD in a χ((2)) or a χ((3))-based fiber-optic entangled-photon source is achieved when the pump bandwidth is half the bandwidth of quantum channel and that the entangled state is degraded gradually with increasing PMD.

we have shown theoretically and experimentally that the degradation of entanglement due to PMD in one of the two optical paths in a quantum communication system can be minimized by reducing the bandwidth of the entangled photon generation pump laser to half the bandwidth of each optical path.

we have studied the effect of PMD in an optical fiber entanglement distribution setup and have shown that the highest PMDs are achieved when the bandwidths of the pump used in the generation of the entangled photons and the entanglement distribution channels are approximately equal.
In summary, our research is concerned with
quantum entanglement in the presence of PMD.
the development of a quantum cryptography system that uses polarization entanglement as a resource.
the development of a fiber optic entanglement source for quantum key distribution (QKD) and the characterization of polarization mode dispersion as a potential source of noise.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the entanglement distribution is not affected by PMD in the quantum channel and the entanglement is degraded only by PMD in one of the classical channels.
the polarization entanglement is not destroyed in the fiber-optic entangled photon source, however, it does suffer from degradation due to the polarization mode dispersion in the optical fiber.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the entanglement distribution is robust to PMD as long as the bandwidth of the entanglement source matches the bandwidth of the optical fiber.
we have demonstrated the first entanglement distribution over fiber with a 100 km long optical path exposed to PMD.

the entangled state is robust against the PMD in a fiber-optics system, and the entanglement can be preserved in a fiber-optical system even when the fiber has a PMD value as high as 0.1 ps/km(1/2) for the pump with a bandwidth of 10 nm.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the PMD tolerance of an optical entanglement distribution network can be significantly increased by careful choice of the pump bandwidth.
the PMD tolerance of a fiber-optic quantum communication system is limited by the pump bandwidth.
polarization mode dispersion in optical fibers can be tolerated to some extent in entanglement distribution systems, and the maximum PMD tolerance depends on the spectral bandwidth of the pump laser.
